claims.value: <cell line>_HIV-1_R7-3_<Env-3xFLAG|Vif-3xFLAG|untagged>_<experiment>_<light|heavy>; 14 source names
claims.evidence: Seven SILAC mixtures, each its own Proteome Discoverer search whose FileInfos lists exactly those raw files: Env I-DIRT forward (2012_04_23_ENV_F1-F10), Env reverse (ENV_R1-R10), Vif I-DIRT forward (2012_02_10_VIF_F1-F9), Vif reverse (VIF_R1-R9), Vif isotope exchange 5/15/60 min (2012_06_28_VIF_<t>min_01-05). PRIDE sample protocol: 'dividing and pooling each lane into 5, 9, or 10 gel fractions for the Vif exchange, Vif-3XFLAG I-DIRT, and Env-3XFLAG I-DIRT experiments'. Each mixture contributes two sources, one per SILAC channel, because the two channels are physically separate cultures/lysates mixed 1:1 before lysis (I-DIRT) or combined on the beads (exchange). The three exchange time points are separate aliquots that were washed, eluted and run separately, so each gets its own source name; the manifest records that the three heavy sources are aliquots of one bead-bound Vif-3xFLAG affinity isolation and the three light sources aliquots of one untagged-infection lysate.

claims.location: comment[label], characteristics[infectious agent strain], characteristics[bait], characteristics[sample type], factor value[bait] rows 1-40 (Env I-DIRT)
claims.value: forward (ENV_F): SILAC light = CEM-SS infected with Env-3xFLAG virus, SILAC heavy = CEM-SS infected with untagged R7/3; reverse (ENV_R): the labels are swapped
claims.evidence: Paper, 'Cell culture for I-DIRT and reverse I-DIRT analyses': 'Sample preparation for I-DIRT analyses used cells infected with the untagged, parental control virus, R7/3, grown in Lys/Arg deficient RPMI-1640 ... supplemented with heavy isotope 13C6 labelled Lys and Arg ... Cells infected with the 3xFLAG-tagged viruses were cultured in media supplemented with Lys and Arg with natural isotopic abundances ... For reverse I-DIRT, the isotopic characteristics of the RPMI media were switched - cells infected with the control virus were grown in the natural carbon isotope while cells infected with a 3xFLAG-tagged virus were cultured in media supplemented with 13C6 labelled Arg and Lys.' Same orientation in 'Quantification of viral-host interactomes via differential isotopic labeling': 'Light CEM (or MT-2) cells were then infected with the Env- or Vif-3xFLAG-tagged virus ... the companion heavy CEM (or MT-2) culture was infected with the untagged WT virus'. PRIDE data protocol: 'Isotope ratios were calculated as light/total for forward I-DIRT experiments or heavy/total for reverse I-DIRT, Vif isotope exchange and Env SILAC experiments'. File letter F/R matches the .msf names EnvHIV_For / EnvHIV_Rev. Data cross-check on the deposited Proteome Discoverer quantification (median light/(light+heavy) of high-confidence rank-1 PSM precursor areas): 2012_04_23_EnvHIV_For: all-PSM median L/(L+H) 0.668 (n=21963); gp160 1.000 (n=457), gp120 1.000 (n=458), gp41_Env 1.000 (n=399), Vif3XFLAG 1.000 (n=17), Q9H497 1.000 (n=13), Q13951 0.632 (n=3), Pr55 1.000 (n=1) | 2012_04_23_EnvHIV_Rev: all-PSM median L/(L+H) 0.400 (n=22413); gp160 0.000 (n=449), gp120 0.000 (n=449), gp41_Env 0.000 (n=354), Vif3XFLAG 0.000 (n=8), Q9H497 0.000 (n=11), Pr55 0.000 (n=18). The 3xFLAG-tagged bait and its specific interactors must sit at ~1 in the channel of the tagged infection and the bulk proteome near 0.5-0.7, which is what these numbers show, so the orientation taken from the Methods is confirmed.

claims.location: comment[label], characteristics[infectious agent strain], characteristics[bait], characteristics[sample type], factor value[bait] rows 41-76 (Vif I-DIRT)
claims.value: forward (VIF_F): SILAC light = MT-2 infected with Vif-3xFLAG virus, SILAC heavy = MT-2 infected with untagged R7/3; reverse (VIF_R): the labels are swapped
claims.evidence: Same I-DIRT protocol as Env: the paper states the labelling was 'performed identically for tagged Vif virus in the context of the restrictive MT-2 cell line'; .msf names VIF_IDIRT_For / VIF_IDIRT_Rev match the file letters F/R. Data cross-check (same measure): 2012_02_10_VIF_IDIRT_For: all-PSM median L/(L+H) 0.580 (n=23371); Vif 1.000 (n=105), Vif3XFLAG 1.000 (n=155), Q13951 1.000 (n=105), Pr55 0.767 (n=136) | 2012_02_10_VIF_IDIRT_Rev: all-PSM median L/(L+H) 0.535 (n=18871); Vif 0.000 (n=121), Vif3XFLAG 0.006 (n=237), Q13951 0.000 (n=120), Pr55 0.296 (n=74). Vif-3xFLAG and its reported specific interactors (CBFbeta/PEBB) are at the tagged-virus end of the ratio, confirming the orientation.

claims.location: comment[label], characteristics[infectious agent strain], characteristics[bait], characteristics[sample type], factor value[bait] rows 77-106 (Vif isotope exchange)
claims.value: SILAC heavy = Vif-3xFLAG complexes affinity-purified from heavy-labelled MT-2 infected with the Vif-3xFLAG virus; SILAC light = lysate of light-labelled MT-2 infected with the untagged virus, added to the beads as competitor
claims.evidence: Paper, 'Competitive isotopic exchange assay for detection of Vif-host dynamic interaction': 'The methodologies for the differential metabolic labelling of MT-2 cells infected with either Vif-3xF (heavy) or the untagged comparator (light) virus were the same as that used in the reverse I-DIRT experiments ... Anti-FLAG M2 mAb conjugated magnetic Dynabeads were then used to affinity purify Vif complexes from the heavy labelled Vif-3xF infected cells. After removing the heavy lysate from the beads, an equal volume of the light labelled lysate prepared from the untagged control infection was added to the beads'. Fig. 4c legend: 'immunoaffinity-isolated, heavy isotope-labelled tagged Vif and heavy isotope-labelled associated proteins were exposed to protein extract of normal (light) peptide'. PRIDE: heavy/total for the 'Vif isotope exchange' experiments. The three exchange .msf files declare QuantificationMethod 'IDIRT (Arg6, Lys6)'. Data cross-check (same measure): 2012_06_28_VIF_Ex5min: all-PSM median L/(L+H) 0.253 (n=16960); Vif 0.000 (n=49), Vif3XFLAG 0.009 (n=100), Pr55 0.258 (n=112). Vif-3xFLAG stays at the heavy end (low L/(L+H)) because only the bead-bound heavy purification carries the bait, confirming heavy = Vif-3xFLAG purification and light = untagged competitor lysate.

claims.value: study sample on the 3xFLAG-tagged-virus channel, negative control on the untagged-virus channel
claims.evidence: In I-DIRT the differentially labelled untagged-R7/3 infection is the control that defines the nonspecific ratio: the paper states 'I_T/(I_T + I_UT) ... is 1 for specific interactors and 0.5 for nonspecific interactors' (I_UT = peptides from the untagged strain) and that the untagged R7/3 is the 'parental control virus'. In the exchange assay the untagged-infection lysate is the competitor control. Terms: study sample PRIDE:0001013 and negative control PRIDE:0000905, both children of PRIDE:0000895 / PRIDE:0001014 and non-obsolete in OLS4.

claims.value: HIV-1 Env-3xFLAG (rows 1-40) / HIV-1 Vif-3xFLAG (rows 41-106) / 'no bait (anti-FLAG affinity enrichment from cells infected with untagged HIV-1 R7/3)' on every untagged-virus row

Paper: replication-competent HIV-1 R7/3 derivatives carrying a 3xFLAG insertion in env or vif, affinity-captured with M2 anti-FLAG Dynabeads; the companion culture is infected with the untagged parental virus and contributes no FLAG bait. claims.value: 1..n within each factor-value group (cell line, bait, exchange time)
claims.evidence: Independent cultures, per spec README.adoc:330 and campaign rule 3. Env: the forward and reverse mixtures are separate infections of separately labelled CEM-SS cultures, so the Env-3xFLAG channel of the forward mixture is replicate 1 and of the reverse mixture replicate 2 (likewise the untagged channel); the paper calls the label swap 'additional biological and technical replicates'. Vif I-DIRT: the same, replicates 1 and 2 per group. Vif exchange: the three time points are aliquots of ONE heavy Vif-3xFLAG purification and ONE light competitor lysate, so each exchange-time group holds exactly one culture and the number is 1 in each; the time point is the factor, not the replicate.

claims.evidence: Campaign rules 1 and 10: sdrf version from spec README.adoc:27; ms-proteomics v1.2.0 from upstream templates.yaml:150 ('latest: 1.2.0') at bigbio/sdrf-templates 7da1747; the template columns are written by sdrf-tools build from the -t flags. Templates chosen: ms-proteomics (LC-MS/MS), human (NCBITaxon 9606), cell-lines (both samples are immortalised lines). clinical-metadata and oncology-metadata are not declared: there are no patient specimens (campaign rule 15).

limitations: The I-DIRT channel orientation is documented by the paper's Methods and the PRIDE ratio definition, and cross-checked against the deposited Proteome Discoverer quantification; no per-file sample sheet was deposited, so the forward/reverse assignment rests on the file-name letters F/R matching the .msf names (EnvHIV_For/EnvHIV_Rev, VIF_IDIRT_For/VIF_IDIRT_Rev) plus that data check.

Supplementary Tables 1-2 and Supplementary Figs 7, 12, 13, 15 of PMC4928716 (per-protein I-DIRT ratios) were not retrieved: the Europe PMC full-text XML endpoint returns HTTP 500 for this PMCID and the supplement is a single NIHMS PDF (NIHMS795262-supplement-Supplemental_1.pdf) behind a bot check that was not bypassed. The PMC OA text/XML of the author manuscript was used instead and carries the full Methods.
characteristics[passage number] is 'not available' (never stated); the paper only says cells were labelled for more than six doublings before infection.

MT-2 (CVCL_2631) carries integrated HTLV-1 proviruses and is an HTLV-1-transformed line; Cellosaurus assigns it no disease, so characteristics[disease] is 'normal' for those rows. The HTLV-1 transformation is not encoded in a column: characteristics[infectious agent] records the experimental HIV-1 infection, and the template has no multi-valued equivalent.
No MS run in this deposit comes from an uninfected culture, so there is no uninfected control arm to annotate; the control channel is the untagged-virus infection.

CEM-SS has no CLO/BTO/EFO class, so characteristics[cell line] keeps the Cellosaurus name and parse_sdrf warns; the CEM-SS donor age 3Y11M is encoded as developmental stage 'child stage (1-4 yo)' (HsapDv:0000265), which is outside the template's EFO list and also warns.
The MT-2 donor age is Cellosaurus '<1D', which the SDRF age pattern cannot express; the row carries 'not available' for age and 'neonate' for developmental stage.
comment[technical replicate] is 1 everywhere on the evidence that each gel fraction was injected once; no instrument-level repeat-injection record was deposited.
